```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(CellTFusion)
```

`CellTFusion` cell group scores can be used as features to predict clinical outcomes with the [`pipeML`](https://github.com/VeraPancaldiLab/pipeML) package:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("VeraPancaldiLab/pipeML")
```

The features of the models are the cell group scores. Cell groups are learned from the data (TF modules, correlations with the deconvolution features, CCA weights), so they must be learned **within each cross-validation fold**: learning them on all the training samples before cross-validation would let the test samples of each fold influence the features and overestimate performance. `prepare_celltfusion_folds()` does this for `pipeML`: in each fold, `CellTFusion()` is run on the training samples only, and the test samples are scored on the resulting cell groups with `compute.test.set()`. The latent factors are a downstream characterization and are not used as features (`project_factors()` projects the cell group scores of new samples onto them when needed).

## **Input data**

Split the example data into a training and a test set. The deconvolution is computed once for all the samples: it is computed independently for each sample, so this does not leak information between samples.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
raw.counts <- CellTFusion::raw.counts.tuto
traitdata  <- CellTFusion::traitdata.tuto

deconv <- multideconv::compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts,
  methods    = c("Quantiseq", "Epidish"),
  normalized = TRUE,
  return     = FALSE
)

index <- caret::createDataPartition(traitdata$Best.Confirmed.Overall.Response, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)

raw.counts_train <- raw.counts[, index]
traitdata_train  <- traitdata[index, ]
deconv_train     <- deconv[index, ]

raw.counts_test  <- raw.counts[, -index]
traitdata_test   <- traitdata[-index, ]
deconv_test      <- deconv[-index, ]
```

## **Training**

Pass `prepare_celltfusion_folds()` as `fold_construction_fun`, and its arguments through `fold_construction_args_fixed`:

- `deconv` — deconvolution of the training samples, in the same order as `features_train`.
- `raw_counts` — count matrix of the training samples, matched to the samples of `deconv` by name (an error is raised if they differ). `pipeML` converts gene names with `make.names()` (e.g. `HLA-A` becomes `HLA.A`); passing the counts keeps the original gene symbols.
- any other `CellTFusion()` argument, e.g. `TF.collection`, `min_module_size` or `corr`.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ml_res <- pipeML::compute_features.training.ML(
  features_train = t(raw.counts_train),
  task_type      = "classification",
  target_var     = traitdata_train$Best.Confirmed.Overall.Response,
  trait.positive = "PD",
  metric         = "AUROC",
  k_folds        = 5,
  n_rep          = 5,
  ncores         = 2,
  fold_construction_fun        = prepare_celltfusion_folds,
  fold_construction_args_fixed = list(deconv     = deconv_train,
                                      raw_counts = raw.counts_train,
                                      TF.collection = "CollecTRI")
)
```

The final model is trained on the cell group scores of all the training samples (cell groups learned on all of them). The corresponding `CellTFusion()` result is returned in `ml_res$Custom_output`.

## **Prediction on an independent cohort**

Score the test samples on the cell groups of `ml_res$Custom_output`, then predict:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
features_test <- data.frame(compute.test.set(ml_res$Custom_output$Processed_deconvolution, ml_res$Custom_output$Cell_groups,
                                              deconv_test = deconv_test))

pred <- pipeML::compute_prediction(
  model          = ml_res$Model,
  test_data      = features_test,
  target_var     = traitdata_test$Best.Confirmed.Overall.Response,
  trait.positive = "PD",
  task_type      = "classification"
)

pred$AUC$AUROC
```

## **Survival outcomes**

The same function is used for survival models, with the follow-up time and event of each sample (the tutorial `traitdata` includes the overall survival: `os` and `censOS`):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
surv_res <- pipeML::compute_features.training.ML(
  features_train = t(raw.counts_train),
  task_type      = "survival",
  time_var       = traitdata_train$os,
  event_var      = traitdata_train$censOS,
  k_folds        = 5,
  n_rep          = 5,
  ncores         = 2,
  fold_construction_fun        = prepare_celltfusion_folds,
  fold_construction_args_fixed = list(deconv = deconv_train, raw_counts = raw.counts_train)
)

features_test <- data.frame(compute.test.set(surv_res$Custom_output$Processed_deconvolution, surv_res$Custom_output$Cell_groups,
                                              deconv_test = deconv_test))

surv_pred <- pipeML::compute_prediction(
  model     = surv_res$Model,
  test_data = features_test,
  task_type = "survival",
  time_var  = traitdata_test$os,
  event_var = traitdata_test$censOS
)

surv_pred$c_index
```

## **Multi-cohort data**

For samples from several cohorts, pass `batch`: the cohort of each training sample, in the same order as `features_train`. `CellTFusion()` then corrects for cohort in each fold (see [Multi-cohort analysis](a6_batch_analysis.html)), and the test samples of each cohort are scored separately, z-scored on their own means and SDs. A cohort with fewer than 10 test samples in a fold gives a warning, as its scores are then based on few samples. With `LODO = TRUE`, `pipeML` stratifies the folds by cohort and outcome (`batch_var`), so that every fold keeps samples of each cohort in its training and test sets:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
ml_res <- pipeML::compute_features.training.ML(
  features_train = t(raw.counts_train),
  task_type      = "classification",
  target_var     = coldata_train$Response,
  trait.positive = "R",
  metric         = "AUROC",
  LODO           = TRUE,
  batch_var      = coldata_train$Cohort,
  fold_construction_fun        = prepare_celltfusion_folds,
  fold_construction_args_fixed = list(deconv     = deconv_train,
                                      raw_counts = raw.counts_train,
                                      batch      = coldata_train$Cohort)
)
```

For a model trained with `batch`, score each new cohort separately with `compute.test.set()`, as its samples are z-scored on their own means and SDs; a warning is given with fewer than 10 samples, and a single sample cannot be scored this way (all its scores would be 0).

**Note:** `prepare_celltfusion_folds()` runs `CellTFusion()` in every fold. Use `do_parallel = TRUE` (and `workers`) in `fold_construction_args_fixed` to compute several folds in parallel (the package must be installed).
